title: multi-model-concurrency-matrix-generator-and-tokenization-fidelity-reporter
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Added a multi-model concurrency matrix generator and a tokenization-fidelity reporter; new baseline datasets and CI perf checks. Non-breaking; opt-in via config.
commits: init: add matrix generator core and CLI glue (aisha)
feat: sample-based tokenization fidelity estimator + serializer (aisha)
test: add unit and integration tests for sampler and reporter (miguel)
ci: wire perf-e2e job and add flamegraph snapshot step (helen)
docs: usage examples and config reference (aisha)
description: Context and motivation: As we onboard more open and proprietary model variants, cross-model interference and tokenization differences are recurring blind spots when we compare latency and quality across workloads. This PR adds two companion tools: a multi-model concurrency matrix generator that synthesizes cross-traffic scenarios and a tokenization-fidelity reporter that quantifies variance introduced by different tokenizers across model families. || Summary of changes: 1) new CLI matrix_generator that builds traffic matrices from a config specifying model mixes, sequence-length distributions, and concurrency envelopes; 2) sampling engine that produces deterministic epochal workloads with priority-prefetch hints for KV-cache priming; 3) tokenization_fidelity reporter that runs a set of prompts through multiple tokenizer implementations, computes per-token alignment and split variance, and serializes compact differential reports for downstream dashboards; 4) small baseline dataset and example notebook; 5) CI perf-e2e pipeline step that takes a snapshot and uploads flamegraphs. || Commits: (see commits list). || Files changed (high level): added generator and sampler python modules, new reporter and serializer, tests, CI perf job, docs and example notebook. || Testing and CI: Local unit test coverage > 92% for new modules; integrated end-to-end perf job included in this PR. The first perf-e2e run failed due to ephemeral quota in CI (gpu-fleet), was retried and passed on second run. Synthetic run against the small baseline shows matrix-level p50/p95 degradation curves and tokenization-induced output divergence metrics. || Performance notes: On a 4-GPU mini cluster (A100-like profile), a 3x model-mix matrix with seq-dist matching production saw a 12% mean increase in queueing latency at high contention compared to single-model baseline; tokenization mismatch (esp. byte-level vs wordpiece) accounted for up to 0.8% difference in average token counts for our prompt set, which propagated non-linearly into generation cost for long completions. Detailed numbers attached in benchmarks/notes. || Backwards compatibility and rollout: All features are opt-in. The matrix generator is a standalone tool under benchmark-lab/tools and will not affect existing workflows until the CI job is enabled. Tokenization reporter output format documented and included an adapter to our telemetry ingestion. || Follow-ups: hook serializer output into the perf dashboard (ENG-7305), extend sampler to emit KV-cache priming artifacts for replay (ENG-7330), and add a multi-region variant to stress routing policies.
review_comments: Miguel Torres: Nice work. Can the sampler produce deterministic runs from seed + epoch? I need that for regression comparisons.
Aisha Patel: Yes — sampler.py accepts --seed and --epoch and will produce the same trace. Added tests to cover deterministic behaviour.
Helen Zhao: CI perf job is great. I saw the first run timeout on cloud quota; can we add a retry wrapper or quicker fallback?
Aisha Patel: Added a lightweight retry and a smaller quick-snapshot path in perf_e2e.yml to run under constrained CI. Kept full snapshot gated behind a self-hosted runner label.
Samir Gupta: Tokenizer wrappers look solid. Suggest adding a CharRNN tokenization baseline to compare with legacy tokenizers for older models.
Aisha Patel: Added an adapter interface for pluggable tokenizer backends; CharRNN baseline left as follow-up (ENG-7338).
Miguel Torres: Approve after CI green and docs link in README.
